Tara: Heads-up — regression flagged by the structured-output eval after yesterday's mix-quant rollout (FP8+INT4 kernels + new batching interleave). eval-run 2026-03-13 shows 3.2% drop in schema-pass and a handful of hallucinated keys in JSON outputs.
Emily: Ugh. Perf looked great though, right? what was the perf delta? :eyes:
Tara: Yes — tokens/sec ~+18% p95 latency down ~12% on the main Llama-variant. But schema failures on our JSON prompt set jumped. Example output attached in the eval run: keys shuffled, stray "metadata.id" appearing, and occasional truncated arrays.
Kyle: Do we have a repro snippet? long context? KV-cache behavior?
Tara: Minimal repro steps in the eval run: 1) model=mix_fp8_int4_v2 2) batching.interleave=true 3) use_kv_cache=true 4) prompt with structured system msg + long convo (~3k tokens). Observed mismatch when kv cache is compacted and reindexed after interleaved batches.
Pranay: Can you paste the profiler / perf counters around the KV ops? interested in "kv.copy" and "kv.shift" counts.
Tara: Sure, from the perf dump (trimmed):
```
[perf] tokens_processed: 8.9e6
[perf] total_ms: 123456
[kv] cache_hits: 7.9e6
[kv] cache_compactions: 234
[kv] kv_shift_ops: 234
[kv] kv_pad_ops: 0
[kernel] chosen: mix_fp8_int4_kernel_v3
[kernel] fallback_count: 12
[latency] p95_ms: 78.3
[throughput] tok_s: 3512
```
Tara: Note: kv_shift_ops spikes correlate with schema failures in the eval.
Emily: That points at misaligned KV indices after interleaved batching. Could be an off-by-one in the batching heuristic when we rebuild KV pointers after a compact.
Kyle: I remember a recent change in batching scheduler: we added interleave to reduce cold-start latency across streams. PR #2415.
Pranay: Exactly — scheduler interleaves multiple requests across the device and then reconstructs per-request KV offsets. If the reconstruction uses a shared buffer with inconsistent stride, mixed-precision kernels might read stale cache slices. FP8 packing makes the stride math tighter, so an index error would manifest now.
Tara: Repro tested by toggling `batching.interleave=false` in the same job — schema pass goes back to baseline. Perf drops ~14% but quality restored.
Kyle: Ok immediate mitigation: revert interleave default in the staging rollout, add a guard in kernel dispatch to detect inconsistent KV lengths and fall back to safe path.
Emily: Also let's add a targeted unit test: create two requests with different seq lengths, force interleave path, then assert per-request KV pointers after compact match expected offsets.
Pranay: I'll take the kernel guard. TBH we should probably assert on the compacted buffer's magic header (lengths+checksum) before the mixed-kernel consumes it. If checksum fails, do a fallback to the FP32-safe kernel and mark a telemetry metric `kv_alignment_fail`.
Tara: Filing the action items: 1) Revert interleave default in staging (Kyle) 2) Kernel guard + telemetry (Pranay) 3) Add regression unit + e2e test (Emily) 4) Run a bisect if needed to find the exact commit in PR #2415 (Tara)
Kyle: Revert done on staging flag, rolling back 2415 -> staging at 1759876580 by deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: deploy-staging: revert batching.interleave=true -> false (PR 2415 rollback) — completed in 15s.
Pranay: I'll push the guard change as a small patch tomorrow, will include `kv_alignment_fail` metric and a counter for how often we fallback.
Emily: I'll add the unit and an e2e harness test that runs the structured eval across the quant matrix (FP8/INT4/INT8 combos) in CI.
Tara: Thanks. After guard + tests, let's run a focused throughput vs quality sweep; we want the perf gain but not at the cost of schema breakage. For now leaving staging without interleave. :+1:
Kyle: Question — do we need to invalidate cached calibrations? could calibration offsets interact?
Pranay: Good call — calibration changes packing layout (scale/zero) but shouldn't change strides. However, we'll re-run calibration when we re-enable interleave to be safe.
Tara: I'll track this in the triage doc and attach the failing examples/ids from the eval run. Short term: rollback done, telemetry + guard in progress, tests planned.
Emily: Thanks team, good catch.
__notes: Document created for dataset; messages are a single continuous thread string as required by agents.md. All fields are strings or list of strings. No title included.
